 Coram : Pravin S. Patil, J.
Date : September 04, 2025.
. Heard.
2.
The Appellant, by way of present Appeal, is challenging the Judgment and order dated 4/8/2017 passed by the learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Mangrulpir in LAC No. 199/2013.
According to the Appellant, delay of 482 days caused in filing the present Appeal before this Court.

3. The reason stated by the Appellant for causing delay is that after the decision of reference court,
the Respondent/Acquiring Body after filing of execution proceeding before the executing court on 17/1/2019 deposited the amount 2/3 7.caf.3128.2019 in fast.5175.2019.odt awarded by the reference court.
As such, the Appellant received the amount of Rs.14,25,931/- in the month of January-2019.
4. Immediately after receipt of the said amount, he has filed the present Appeal before this Court.
However, Appellant being an agriculturist, was not aware of period of limitation and as a consequences, delay of 482 days is caused in filing the present Appeal.

5. Per contra, learned Counsel appearing for the Respondent No.1 vehemently opposed the application stating that the Applicant is not only cultivator, but he is also in service, as can be seen from the cause-title of the application.
Therefore, the reason put-forth by the Appellant in the Baburao Dadarao Solanke vs Executive Engineer, Minor Irrigation ... on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97304629/

sentences.text: 1 matter not found trustworthy.
6. I have gone through the submission made by the parties.
It is clear that present Appellant is an agriculturist and his land has been acquired by the Respondent No.1.
Considering the fact that the land being acquired by the Authority, immediate compensation was required to be deposited at the instance of Respondent in the matter.

However, in the present case, after filing of the execution proceedings, the amount has been deposited by the Respondent No.1.
7.
Therefore, by accepting the reason put-forth by the 3/3 7.caf.3128.2019 in fast.5175.2019.odt present Appellant, it is a fit case to condone the delay.

However, as the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of New Okhla Industrial Development Authority V/s Rameshwar @ Ramesh Chandra Sharma (dead) through Legal Heir and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1599 , it is made clear that the present Appellant shall not be entitled to any statutory benefits including interest payable under the Land Acquisition Act on the enhanced amount of compensation for the period of delay of 482 days caused in filing Appeal.
8. Civil Application stands disposed of in above terms.
